thread.title: Close Update: Stocks Slide With Tech-Sector Selloff Handing Nasdaq Third Straight Loss

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Stocks Slide With Tech-Sector Selloff Handing Nasdaq Third Straight Loss
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street faltered under a tech-sector selloff Monday that handed the Nasdaq Composite its third consecutive loss and saw heavyweights in the group push deeper into the red.
Gains in the telecom sector and energy stocks helped offset some of the 1.8% tech loss on the Standard & Poor's 500, but declines in Caterpillar ( CAT ) accelerated late in the session, dragging about half of the blue chips on the Dow Jones Industrial Average into declining territory.
Facebook ( FB ) fell 2.2% to the lowest in more than three months on continued weakness in the stock after its disappointing results last week. Netflix ( NFLX ) dropped 5.7%, Alphabet ( GOOGL ) lost 1.8% and Amazon.com ( AMZN ) dropped 2.1%. Apple (AAPL) slipped 0.6% as investors awaited the tech giant's results late Tuesday.
Tech shares had rallied this year, gaining about 14% on the S&P compared with the broader measure's 5.4% year-to-date rise. The Nasdaq hit a record high last week but the selloff that emerged has sent it to the lowest levels since July 5.
Caterpillar reported better-than-expected quarterly earnings earlier Monday, but said sales missed views and the heavy-equipment maker will raise prices to offset tariffs costs. The stock ended down about 2%. Also among the blue chips, American Express (AXP) lost 2.9% after the Wall Street Journal said the company raised currency conversion rates for business clients without warning them in a bid to boost revenue and employee commission.
While earnings have taken much of the attention lately, focus will pivot to the economic front, with a Federal Reserve rate decision Wednesday and July non-farm payrolls on Friday. The Fed is widely expected to keep rates on hold. Financials were up 0.1% on the S&P 500, while the day's best gain came from a 2% rise in telecoms and 0.8% advance in energy as oil prices climbed.
